A primer on comfort stops
This article is for anyone flying with an animal
Companion Animal Travel Desk

Comfort Stops for Companion Animal Travel

Comfort stops help an animal stay settled during travel when a planned pause is allowed and safe. They are part of careful trip planning, not a casual break. Use them only when the route, airport layout, and handling conditions support a calm stop.

Before travel, make sure the animal is ready for transport and that all required documents are in order. <<FACT F093>> Keep your carrier secure, leave enough room for normal movement, and avoid adding loose items that can shift during handling. Water should be offered in a controlled way, and food should be limited when advised by the travel process so the animal does not become upset in transit.

At the airport, follow crew directions and keep the animal under control at all times. Sudden noise, crowding, and rapid movement can increase stress, so speak quietly and move steadily. If the animal shows signs of distress, tell the crew at once and wait for guidance before taking any action. Never open a carrier except when a crew member says it is safe to do so.

If a comfort stop is needed after a delay, after a long handoff, or during a special service step, the passenger coordinator will explain what can be done and what must remain unchanged. <<FACT F102>> Report any injury, escape attempt, or equipment failure without delay so the matter can be reviewed and logged correctly.

Travelers such as Gabriel Fischer and Lucas Lee should keep copies of the animal's documents close at hand and use the same carrier throughout the journey unless the crew directs otherwise. Roxie, like any companion animal, should be monitored for heat, anxiety, and fatigue from check-in through arrival. Calm handling reduces the chance of avoidable incident.

For more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways before departure.
